messages:
Maya: Heads-up — CI and canary telemetry showing a sudden p99 token latency jump in us-west2 on A10 pools after merge-4010. Appears correlated with increased KV cache evictions and NIC retransmits. Can we triage? :eyes:

Arjun: I'm seeing the same in the perf dashboard. p99 from ~120ms -> 450ms on text-gen route (seq 256). H100 clusters are flat. L4 pools slightly elevated but not as bad as A10.

Sam: Noted. Any kernel-picker changes in that merge? I remember it switched the kernel selection policy to prefer "batch-fused" kernels under medium batch sizes.

Maya: Right — merge-4010 introduced adaptive kernel fallback + new batching heuristics. Hypothesis: on A10 the fused kernel causes KV cache alignment issues leading to more frequent spill/evict. NIC counters show TX retries spiking.

Kelly: Sharing snippets from canary logs:
```
[canary-3] kvcache.evictions/sec=78 -> 510
[canary-3] net.tx_retransmits=124 -> 640
[canary-3] kernel=batch-fused v=1.2.0
```

Noah: I started a short experiment: pinned the runtime to kernel v1.1.4 and disabled batch-fused in canary-3. Early signals: p99 dropped back to ~140ms and evictions fell to ~60/s. So that's a strong signal.

Arjun: Good. What about CPU utilization / GPU stalls? Could be a NIC-driver interaction when fused kernel changes memory layout.

Sam: I profiled a sample trace (`perf script` attached). KV cache hot set resizing causes extra host<->device copies at sequence boundaries with fused kernel. On A10, the DMA scheduler seems to push more retransmits when memcpy patterns change.

Maya: Given rollback risk, recommend halting the rollout to remaining regions and reverting merge-4010 from canary. Deploy-bot, please pause the canary rollout and block further merges referencing kernel-picker.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused for canary groups 3..5. CI: merge-4010 marked as rollout-blocked by Maya at 1861209930.

Kelly: I'll open an immediate revert PR and run a focused CI job that exercises long-tail sequences and KV cache churn. Also will add NIC retransmit counters to perf-gate.

Sam: For long-term: we should add per-hardware kernel selection rules. A10 needs alignment-aware kernels or a fallback path that avoids batch-fused for sequences < 512 when KV cache churn > threshold.

Noah: Agree. Also propose adding a quick guard: if net.tx_retransmits > 200 within 60s, switch to kernel v1.1.4 automatically and notify.

Arjun: I'll take ownership of the rollback PR and the guard instrumentation. Maya, can you coordinate with platform to validate on other A10 clusters (us-east1/usw2) before unblocking?

Maya: Yep — running validation runs now. Will post results shortly. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Kelly: FYI — CI perf job 1845520022 failed similarly earlier today but was noisy and dismissed. Looks like that was the same root cause.

Maya: Good catch. Let's treat this as high priority. If rollback fixes canary we'll merge revert and cut a patch release. Otherwise we'll consider kernel-picker config toggle.

Arjun: Update — initial validation on us-east1 A10 shows p99 improvement after pin; preparing revert PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4527

Maya: Thanks. Leaving rollout on hold until PR merges and we run canary window. Closing loop when done. :white_check_mark:
